Acne: Keep the skin gently clean and avoid squeezing pimples.
Avoid harsh scrubbing and products that irritate the skin.
Seek professional advice if acne is severe, painful, or persistent.
Eczema: Keep the skin moisturized with a fragrance-free moisturizer.
Seek medical advice for severe, infected, or persistent symptoms.
Psoriasis: Keep affected skin moisturized and avoid scratching.
Try to identify and avoid personal flare triggers.
Seek professional medical advice for diagnosis and treatment.
Contact Dermatitis: Stop using the suspected irritating product if safe to do so.
Gently wash the affected area and avoid further exposure.
Seek medical advice if the reaction is severe or does not improve.
Ringworm: Keep the affected area clean and dry.
Avoid sharing towels, clothing, or personal items.
A clinician or pharmacist can advise on appropriate antifungal treatment.
Urticaria: Avoid a known trigger if one is identified.
A cool compress may help reduce discomfort.
Seek urgent medical care for swelling of the lips/tongue or breathing difficulty.
Scabies: Avoid close skin-to-skin contact until evaluated and treated.
Wash bedding and clothing according to appropriate medical guidance.
Seek medical advice because specific treatment is usually required.
Impetigo: Keep sores clean and avoid picking or scratching them.
Do not share towels, clothing, or personal items.
Seek medical advice because bacterial skin infections may need treatment.
Vitiligo: Protect depigmented areas from excessive sun exposure.
Use sun protection on areas with reduced pigment.
See a dermatologist for confirmation and treatment options.
Rosacea: Identify and avoid personal triggers such as heat or spicy foods.
Seek professional advice for persistent facial redness or eye symptoms.
Folliculitis: Keep the area clean and avoid friction or close shaving while irritated.
Avoid picking or squeezing the bumps.
Seek medical advice if there is spreading redness, significant pain, fever, or persistence.
Seborrheic Dermatitis: Use gentle skin and hair-care products and avoid scratching.
Keep affected areas clean and follow pharmacist or clinician advice for suitable products.
Seek professional advice if symptoms are persistent or severe.
